terms.title: Job words explained
terms.lead: What the words on job listings mean, in plain language. Ask the employer or your recruiter if anything on a listing is still unclear.
items: CTC (cost to company)
Everything the employer spends on you in a year: salary, PF the company pays, bonuses and other benefits. Your take-home pay is less than the CTC.
LPA (lakhs per annum)
Pay for a year, in lakhs of rupees. 3 LPA is ₹3,00,000 a year, about ₹25,000 a month before deductions.
In-hand salary
What reaches your bank account each month, after PF, tax and other deductions.
PF (Provident Fund) and ESI
PF is retirement savings: part of your salary, and the employer adds the same. ESI is health insurance for lower-paid workers. Both are deducted from pay where they apply.
Notice period
How long you must keep working at your current job after you resign, before you can start a new one.
Full-time, part-time and contract
Full-time is a regular job, usually 8–9 hours a day. Part-time is fewer hours. Contract work is for a fixed time, often through an agency.
Daily wage / gig
Paid by the day or by the task, often without a fixed monthly salary.
Shift
The hours you work. A night shift is overnight; a rotational shift changes from week to week.
On-site, hybrid and remote
On-site means you work at the workplace every day. Hybrid is some days at the workplace and some at home. Remote is from home.
Walk-in interview
Go to the address on the given day and time without booking. Take your documents and a copy of your resume.
Fresher
Someone looking for their first job, with no work experience yet.
Probation
The first few months of a job, when the employer and you check that the job is a good fit.
Openings
How many people the employer wants to hire for this job.
terms.warning: A genuine employer never asks you for money, an OTP, a UPI PIN or your bank password to apply or to get a job.

a11y.title: Accessibility
a11y.lead: We want everyone to be able to find work and hire on {site}, including people who use a keyboard, a screen reader, voice input or larger text.
done: Every page works with a keyboard alone, with a visible focus outline and a link to skip to the content.
Form fields have labels, errors are listed at the top of the form and next to the field, and nothing depends on colour alone.
Pages can be zoomed to 200% and read on small phones without losing content.
Animations stop when your device asks for reduced motion.
Pages are available in English and Hindi, and you can search for jobs in Hindi and Telugu.
Job listings can be read aloud, and you can speak instead of typing where your browser supports it. Typing always works too.
a11y.limitsTitle: What we are still working on
limits: Employer and team pages are in English only.
Some older pages have not yet been checked with every screen reader.
PDF documents such as invoices may not be fully accessible. Ask us for another format.
a11y.contactText: If something on {site} is hard to use, email {email} or call {phone}. Tell us the page and what happened, and we'll help you apply or hire another way while we fix it.
a11y.standard: We are working towards the Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.2, level AA. This statement was last reviewed on {date}.
